text: This chapter covered three genuinely different backup mechanisms, not one idea with three names. This lesson's is the third: on-prem or VM-hosted SQL Server, backing up straight to Azure Blob Storage instead of local disk.

The syntax is almost identical to what you already know — BACKUP DATABASE TO URL instead of TO DISK, after a one-time CREATE CREDENTIAL step. Every restore-chain rule from earlier in this chapter still applies exactly as-is.

Recovery point objective is how much data loss is acceptable if disaster strikes right now, and it's a direct consequence of backup frequency — log backups every 15 minutes means an RPO of up to 15 minutes, nightly-only means up to 24 hours.

On-prem to local disk restores fastest but isn't durable unless copied off-site. Azure SQL Database's automatic backups are already geo-durable with an RPO fixed by Microsoft. Backup to URL is the deliberate middle ground the DBA still controls.
Chapter 13 is done. Chapter 14, High Availability and Disaster Recovery — eight lessons, matching the real exam's 20 to 25 percent weight — picks up exactly here, with RPO's counterpart RTO.
